I could not find any feasible placement satisfying all rules. Reasoning summary:

- Destination v2 has only one link: (v2–v9). Therefore the path into the destination must come from v9. That forces the last VNF (f4) to be placed on v9 (if the VNF is placed on the penultimate node) or on v2 (if f4 is colocated with destination). Either choice creates an unavoidable connectivity requirement:
  - If f4 is on v9, the chain must start at source v9, leave v9 to visit f1 and f2, then return to v9 as f4. To return to v9 the VNF immediately before f4 must be a neighbor of v9 (only v1 or v3). But constructing a length-4 distinct-VNF chain v9 -> f1 -> f2 -> (v1 or v3) -> v9 is impossible because v1 and v3 do not share a common neighbor (other than v9), so you cannot place the required distinct f1/f2 nodes with the needed edges.
  - If f4 is placed on v2, then the VNF before it (f3) must be on v9 (the only neighbor of v2). That requires both v9 to host a VNF (f3) and also be the source, forcing the chain to leave v9 and return to v9 earlier; again, the local connectivity around v9/v1/v3 prevents placing the needed distinct f1 and f2 nodes with the required edges.

- I also checked CPU and bandwidth feasibility on candidate nodes/links: node capacities are sufficient individually for the VNFs, and many links have capacity >=71, but the topological constraints around v9/v2 prevent a simple path that visits four distinct VNF nodes in order while starting at v9 and ending at v2.

Because of these topology constraints there is no valid placement/path that meets all conditions (distinct VNF nodes, chain order, and connectivity to reach v2).
